stem: OWD for Installation is Private. Who can see a record owned by user A?

options.text: User A, and users above A in the role hierarchy if hierarchies are enabled
Only users with the same profile

explanation: With Private OWD, the owner and (with Grant Access Using Hierarchies) users above them can see it, plus anyone given extra access.

stem: Which statement about sharing rules is true?

options.text: They can only open up access, never restrict it
They can make a record more private than OWD
They can share records with a profile

explanation: Sharing rules grant additional access. They cannot restrict below OWD and they do not target profiles.

stem: Everyone should see Opportunities, but only the owner should be able to edit. Which OWD setting is right?
explanation: Public Read Only lets everyone see records while only the owner (and those given edit access) can change them.

stem: What does the role hierarchy grant?

options.text: Record access up the management chain

explanation: Roles affect record access only. Object and field permissions come from profiles and permission sets.

stem: Manual sharing is available when the OWD of an object is:
explanation: Manual sharing opens access beyond the baseline, so it is useful when OWD is Private or Public Read Only.

stem: Which OWD setting means access is determined by the parent record?
explanation: Controlled by Parent makes child records follow the access of their parent, as with Contact on Account in some configurations.

stem: Which TWO targets can a sharing rule share records with? (Choose 2)
explanation: Sharing rules target roles, roles and subordinates, and public groups. Profiles and permission sets are not valid targets.

stem: What does the Grant Access Using Hierarchies setting do for an object?

options.text: Lets managers access records owned by their subordinates
Lets subordinates see their managers' records
Allows users to share without owning

explanation: With it on, users higher in the role hierarchy get access to records owned by users below them.

stem: Public Read/Write/Transfer is an OWD option for which objects?
explanation: The Transfer variant of Public Read/Write is available for Leads and Cases.

stem: A sales rep can open the Installation tab but sees an empty list, and the OWD is Private. Which is the most likely reason?

options.text: They own no installations and nothing has been shared with them

explanation: With a Private OWD a user sees only records they own or that are shared with them. An empty list usually means no record meets either condition.

stem: Which statement about the role hierarchy is true?

options.text: It gives record access upward but not object or field permissions
It can restrict access below the OWD
It lets you share with a profile

explanation: Roles only extend record access. A manager still needs object permission from a profile or permission set.

stem: A custom object's OWD is Private. Should Grant Access Using Hierarchies be on?

options.text: It is optional for custom objects, so turn it on if managers need the access
It only applies to standard objects

explanation: For custom objects you can choose whether managers inherit access through the hierarchy. On standard objects it is always on.

stem: Which target can a sharing rule NOT use?
explanation: Sharing rules share with roles, roles and subordinates, and public groups. A profile is not a sharing target.

stem: A criteria-based rule shares Installations where Type is Commercial with a group as Read Only. The OWD is Public Read/Write. What happens?

options.text: The rule adds nothing because the OWD already gives more access

explanation: Sharing rules can only add access. They cannot reduce what the OWD already grants.

stem: What happens to a manual share when the record owner changes?
explanation: Manual shares are lost when ownership changes, so they are weak for long-term needs.

stem: A rep needs access to one customer account for a week. Which is the best fit?

options.text: Manual sharing or an account team
A new role for the whole department

explanation: One record for a short time is an exception, which is what manual sharing or a team handles.

stem: The Marketing department needs to see all Cases owned by Support, permanently, with read access. Which is best?

options.text: A sharing rule to a Marketing public group
Changing the OWD of Case to Public Read/Write

explanation: A recurring group-level need is exactly what a sharing rule is for. The other options are too narrow or too broad.

stem: Which permission gives a user access to every record of one object regardless of sharing?
explanation: View All and Modify All on an object bypass sharing for that object. View All Data does it for every object.

stem: What does implicit sharing give a user who can see a contact?

options.text: Read access to the contact's parent account

explanation: Access to a child record gives the user read access to its parent account.

objective: Use manual sharing, teams and Apex sharing
stem: Where do developers see the share records created by Apex managed sharing for a custom object?
explanation: Each object with sharing has a share table, named ObjectName__Share for custom objects.

stem: After the admin changes an object's OWD, what runs in the background?
explanation: Changing the sharing model recalculates access and can take time on large orgs.

stem: Which TWO belong in the troubleshooting steps for a user who cannot see a record? (Choose 2)

options.text: Check the OWD and whether they are above the owner in the hierarchy

explanation: Object permission and the OWD plus hierarchy come first. Layouts affect fields on screen and browser history rarely matters.

stem: Which TWO can a sharing rule share records with? (Choose 2)
explanation: Targets are roles, roles and subordinates, and public groups.

stem: Which OWD applies to the child in a master-detail relationship?
explanation: The child has no owner field and inherits access from the master record.

stem: Which is the first thing to try when everyone should see an object but only owners should edit it?

options.text: Set the OWD to Public Read Only
Create a sharing rule for each department
Use manual sharing for all records

explanation: One OWD setting meets the need. Sharing rules and manual shares would be needless work.

stem: A user can see an account in a list but does not own it and has no sharing rule. What could explain it?

options.text: Implicit sharing from a child contact or opportunity they can access

explanation: Access to a child record can give read access to the parent account.

objective: Use manual sharing, teams and Apex sharing
stem: Which feature shares accounts by region and is built for sales structures that change often?
explanation: Territory management assigns accounts to territories and shares them to the people in those territories.
